indication: [AGE]-year-old [GENDER] presenting with chronic cough and weight loss. Evaluate for active tuberculosis versus lung malignancy.
technique: ** Multidetector CT of the chest was performed with intravenous contrast administration. Axial images were acquired from the thoracic inlet to the adrenal glands. Multiplanar reformations were reviewed.
findings:
**
The lungs demonstrate evidence of prior granulomatous disease. There is extensive volume loss and architectural distortion involving the right upper lobe, characterized by dense fibrotic bands and traction bronchiectasis. Within this area of scarring, there is a well-defined, contrast-enhancing saccular structure measuring approximately 8 mm in diameter arising from a segmental branch of the right pulmonary artery, consistent with a pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysm. No evidence of acute consolidation, centrilobular nodules, or tree-in-bud opacities is seen to suggest active endobronchial spread of infection. No suspicious pulmonary nodules or masses are identified in either lung.
The pleural spaces are clear. There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax. The pericardium is thin and unremarkable, and the heart size is within normal limits.
The mediastinum shows no significant lymphadenopathy; the hilar and mediastinal nodes are not enlarged. The trachea and mainstem bronchi are patent. The esophagus is normal in caliber.
Within the visualized upper abdomen, there is a small, simple hepatic cyst measuring 1 cm in the right lobe of the liver. A few small, non-obstructing renal cortical cysts are noted bilaterally. The adrenal glands are unremarkable. The bony structures of the thoracic cage show mild degenerative changes of the thoracic spine.
conclusion:
**
Findings are consistent with sequelae of post-primary pulmonary tuberculosis, specifically right upper lobe fibrosis and volume loss. There is an associated pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysm within the scarred region of the right upper lobe. No evidence of active tuberculosis or malignancy.
